title: Apple Crisp
description: Tender cinnamon apples baked under a crunchy oat and brown sugar topping until the juices bubble and thicken.
scaleNote: This fills a {len 9x9 in} or 2-quart baking dish. For 16 servings use a {len 9x13 in} dish and bake 5 to 10 minutes longer.

image.alt: Illustration of a baking dish of apple crisp with a crumbly golden topping, beside an apple

items.prep: peeled, cored and sliced {len 1/4 in} thick
items.note: about {qty 2 1/2 lb}; a mix of tart and sweet is best

steps.text: Heat the oven to {temp 375F oven} with a rack in the middle. Set the baking dish on the rimmed baking sheet to catch any drips.
In a large bowl, toss the apple slices with the lemon juice, then with the sugar, cinnamon and cornstarch until evenly coated. Spread them in the baking dish.
In another bowl, mix the flour, oats, brown sugar, cinnamon and salt. Pour in the melted butter and stir with a fork until everything is moist and forms small clumps.
Scatter the topping evenly over the apples, squeezing some of it into larger clumps as you go.
Bake until the topping is deep golden and the juices bubble thickly around the edges, {time 40-45 min}. If the topping browns before the juices bubble, lay a sheet of foil loosely over the dish.
Let the crisp cool for {time 15 min} so the juices thicken. Serve warm, with a scoop of ice cream if you like.

notes: Good baking apples hold their shape: Granny Smith and Honeycrisp are a reliable pair.
Make ahead: mix the topping and refrigerate it in a covered container for up to 3 days, then assemble and bake.
Leftovers keep, covered, in the fridge for up to 4 days. Rewarm in a {temp 350F oven} for about {time 15 min notimer} to re-crisp the top.
